conventions.convention: Reverse time is u=T−t. K_{u,v} takes the forward state at T−u to the forward state at T−v, with numerator p_{T−v}(x)q(T−v,x;T−u,y) and denominator p_{T−u}(y).
The forward generator is b·∇+(1/2)a:D² with a=σσᵀ. The reverse drift is −b+div(a)+a∇log(p), where div(a)_i=Σ_j ∂_j a_{ij}.
In the bounded-start construction, B_u=tilde W_{T−u}−tilde W_T. Right-endpoint integrals in forward time become ordinary left-endpoint Itô integrals after reversing time.
At the Gaussian data endpoint p_0 denotes the probability measure μ, not a Lebesgue density. K_{u,T} is a posterior kernel integrated against μ.
Gaussian score and state-Lipschitz assertions are restricted to forward times [ε,T], with 0<ε<T; endpoint convergence makes no score claim at zero.
The occupation lemma uses a=(1/2)ΣΣᵀ, rather than the covariance matrix convention used by the reversal theorems. Its absolute continuity concerns spacetime Lebesgue measure.
The predictable reconstruction lemma permits an arbitrary filtration and merely predictable σ; the Gaussian reversal theorem states its Brownian conclusion in the usual augmentation.

load_bearing.statement: Under AC, a continuous local martingale started at zero has continuous quadratic variation, obtained uniformly in probability along every deterministic vanishing-mesh partition sequence, and M²−[M] is a local martingale. Polarization gives covariations and the stated product formula. A continuous finite-variation local martingale is constant.

For the nonnegative bounded globally Lipschitz semiconvex f, λ>0, and normalized controls specified in the Statement, there exists the asserted bounded Lipschitz semiconvex v with bounded weak time and spatial derivatives, satisfying the normalized Bellman equation almost everywhere, S≥0, H≥0 and S det(H)=(f/(d+1))^(d+1). Each fixed-control inequality also holds distributionally, and v satisfies the stated smooth-supersolution comparison.

Assume AC. For each d≥1 and nonnegative smooth compactly supported spacetime f, there exists bounded nonnegative globally Lipschitz v with bounded weak v_t, D_xv and D_x²v, satisfying ||v||∞≤C_d||f||_{d+1}, |D_xv|≤v almost everywhere, and v_t+A:D_x²v−(1+tr A)v+(det A)^(1/(d+1))f≤0 simultaneously for every constant symmetric positive semidefinite A, distributionally and almost everywhere.

For the usual filtered Brownian Itô process in the Statement, with finite initial state, pathwise finite drift variation and diffusion energy, and (1/2)ΣΣᵀ≥κI almost everywhere, every stop γ≤T satisfying E∫_0^γ(|β_s|+tr a_s)ds<∞ has spacetime occupation measure μ_γ(E)=E∫_0^γ1_E(s,Z_s)ds absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure. Such stops exhaust T; no moment assumption on Z_0 is required.

Under its classical forward-density, positivity and coefficient hypotheses, an auxiliary reverse Brownian Itô process started from p_T, with the stated drift and bracket density, finite pathwise coefficient integrals and absolutely continuous stopped spacetime occupation measures, has the same path law as X_{T−u}. It consequently has the Bayes kernels, and the actual reversal solves the stated local martingale problem.

Assume AC. On a finite horizon and an arbitrary filtration, let M be a continuous adapted local martingale started at zero, and σ a predictable invertible square matrix process with bounded inverse and finite pathwise squared energy. If [M]_t=∫_0^tσσᵀds, localized bracket-energy completion defines B=∫σ^−1dM, Brownian in the given filtration, with M=∫σdB up to indistinguishability.

The base positive-density and classical forward-equation hypotheses give the Bayes reversed kernels and formal adjoint product identity. The additional local weighted integrability, actual backward-Kolmogorov and spatial adjoint hypotheses give the true compact-test martingale conclusion. The unconditional formal candidate identity alone makes no martingale or pointwise transition-quotient assertion.

For the continuous nonexplosive Markov diffusion satisfying all the Statement's Brownian, path-integrability, uniform nonsingularity, positive classical density, analytic and well-posed reverse martingale-problem hypotheses, Y_u=X_{T−u} has the displayed Bayes kernels and solves dY_u=[−b+div(a)+a∇log(p)]_{T−u}(Y_u)du+σ_{T−u}(Y_u)dB_u, with B Brownian in its natural reversed filtration.

For the stated compactly supported Gaussian smoothing setup and 0<ε<T, Y_u=X_{T−u} admits the reverse SDE with drift g(T−u)²∇log p_{T−u} and dispersion g(T−u)I in the usual augmented reversed filtration. The drift has the stated global Lipschitz and linear-growth bounds on the truncated interval. E|Y_{T−ε}−X_0|²=dv(ε) and W₂(Law(Y_{T−ε}),μ)≤√(dv(ε)); no score regularity at zero is asserted.

concerns.concern: F1 states that an adapted continuous process is predictable and applies this directly to H=σ^−1, although the Statement imposes no usual-filtration assumption or everywhere-continuous representative. The cited lem-adapted-continuous-processes-are-progressively-measurable explicitly requires everywhere-continuous paths, or an initial-measurable full continuity event for its normalization. Step 1.1 also obtains a 'continuous adapted version' from an almost-sure uniformly convergent subsequence without specifying its values on the exceptional event. A predictable representative defined by pointwise limits of the already-used original-adapted left-step approximations closes this version issue; the later predictable reconstruction lemma spells out this construction.

The Tang–Zhao citation names 'Y. Tang' and 'Section 2.2'. The linked paper identifies its first author as Wenpin Tang and places the reversal formula in Section 2, Theorem 2.1, equation (2.3), with the heuristic argument on PDF pp. 4–5: [Tang and Zhao](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.07487). The same incorrect Section 2.2 locator occurs in def-reversed-transition-kernels-for-diffusions, lem-reversed-kernels-and-generator-identity, def-bayes-reversed-gaussian-smoothing-kernels, thm-markov-diffusion-reversal-by-bayes-kernels and lem-reversed-smoothing-generator-and-martingale. The description of the source argument as heuristic is faithful.

The exact endpoint mean-square and W₂ claims match their supplier.

Read the score definition, probability-flow theorem and predictor-corrector algorithm. The algorithm explicitly applies thm-markov-diffusion-reversal-by-bayes-kernels after translating [ε,T] to [0,T−ε], retaining AC, relative Brownian increments, coefficient integrability, uniform nonsingularity, positive classical densities and the reverse martingale-problem assumption. The probability-flow theorem supplies its own continuity-equation proof and makes no unsupported path-law claim.
